requirements.text: raise a new incident to capture this operational impact and link it to the affected change request, documenting that the issue is causing a delay due to incorrect ownership and configuration data
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND caller_id = 'USER_041' AND configuration_item = 'CI_006' AND assigned_to = 'USER_031' AND assignment_group = 'GROUP_004' AND change_request = 'CHG_020' AND status = 'new' AND description LIKE '%incorrect%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_101 after INC_100); the only incident the task creates
the affected change request is CHG_020 'Migrate Marketing Share to Cloud', the only change about the marketing file share; the benchmark's 'CHG_20' is no id in the seed, so the value is repaired
caller_id USER_041 kept from the benchmark check: the request names no caller and the acting user, who requested the change, is the user affected (policy 3.1)
configuration_item CI_006 kept from the benchmark check: the change's CI (status in_use, so it may be linked under policy 5.1); not fixed by request or policy

assigned_to USER_031 and assignment_group GROUP_004 kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the request reassigns the change, not the incident); USER_031 is an active manager and a member of GROUP_004, so policy 3.2 allows it; the leading space in ' GROUP_004' is repaired
status new from the policy default (3.1)

description LIKE '%incorrect%': the benchmark's three unparenthesised OR alternatives folded into one containment on the word the request uses ('incorrect ownership'), since a disjunction is not a cell predicate
impact and urgency are mandatory under this policy but the request fixes no value and the benchmark tests none, so they are not cells

requirements.text: Update the change request by reassigning it to the L2 Service Desk team, specifically to one of the manager
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM change WHERE change_id = 'CHG_020' AND requested_by = 'USER_041' AND configuration_item = 'CI_006' AND assigned_to = 'USER_031' AND assignment_group = 'GROUP_004'
assumptions: L2 Service Desk is GROUP_004 (L1 Service Desk, GROUP_003, is the near match); its only member with role manager is Robin Monroe, USER_031, active
the group's manager_id USER_002 is a reporter and not a member, so policy 3.2 rules them out
requested_by and configuration_item are the seed's values, kept from the benchmark check; the change is in assigned_to (USER_052 on the seed) and assignment_group (GROUP_008 on the seed)

requirements.text: correct the associated configuration item by updating its cost to 12,000

assumptions: the associated CI is the change's configuration_item CI_006 (FileShare-01, cost 9000 on the seed)

verify_incident_created.evidence: right in substance (one incident for the misassigned change, linked to CHG_020) but wrong in values: change_request 'CHG_20' is no id in the seed (the marketing share change is CHG_020), assignment_group ' GROUP_004' carries a leading space, and the three description LIKE alternatives are unparenthesised ORs, so as written the AND conditions bind only the first and the query counts any incident mentioning workflow stoppage or marketing (0 on this seed by luck); repaired to CHG_020, GROUP_004, one containment on 'incorrect' (the request's word), anchored to the new row INC_101

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the incident, the change, the CI cost and all five dispositions (verify_incident_created repaired the same way by both). disagreement: notification to the previous assignee: A selects by email = 'casey.green@servicenow.com' AND message LIKE '%marketing%', B by incident_id = 'INC_101' AND email; kept B's because notification.incident_id is NOT NULL, no seed incident links CHG_020 and INC_101 is the only incident the task concerns, so incident and recipient is the natural key and B's predicate is the tighter of two right ones. disagreement: notification to the new assignee: the same difference (A by email and message, B by incident_id = 'INC_101' and email); kept B's for the same reason. disagreement: stay on change CHG_010 and CHG_014 (B only); kept because both are rows a loose search for the marketing file-share change sweeps in (CHG_010's description names a marketing vendor; CHG_014 shares CI_006 and assignee USER_052 with CHG_020), so the stay marks the boundary of the change the request names. disagreement: stay on configuration_item CI_071 cost 900 (B only); kept because CI_071 'Marketing iPad' is the other CI a search on 'marketing' returns, a boundary of 'the associated configuration item'. Judgements both passes made the same way and the merge keeps: 'link it to the affected change request' is the incident's change_request column, which the benchmark tests (a change_request_mapping row would be a second way to link, and no listed tool writes that table); this policy (4afd943b) makes impact and urgency mandatory with no defaults, so they are not cells and an agent following it literally may halt on the missing fields, which the benchmark does not expect; the acting user USER_041 is an admin. Least sure: the description containment on 'incorrect' (an agent may document the delay in other words, or in short_description) and the incident's assigned_to and assignment_group, kept only because the benchmark tests them.
revised: the note on the CHG_010 and CHG_014 stay justified it by appeal to an outside rule; it now states the reason itself (both changes border the change the request names).
